newsitem.title: USA: Jury process outlined for Florida suit vs tobacco.
newsitem.headline: Jury process outlined for Florida suit vs tobacco.

text.p: The trial judge in the state of Florida's lawsuit against the tobacco industry on Wednesday said a jury would be selected from a pool of 300 prospects, with each side allowed to dismiss 39 of them without explanation.
Palm Beach County Circuit Court Judge Harold Cohen also gave each side 54 more unrestricted challenges to be used in selecting alternate jurors.
Six jurors and an undetermined number of alternates will be chosen for the trial, scheduled to begin on August 4.

Jury selection could take as long a month, lawyers said. Testimony may take three months or longer, before the jury is asked to decide on Florida's suit, which seeks $17 billion and other money to pay for treating sick smokers.

Cohen ordered that 300 people be summoned to the Palm Beach County Courthouse to fill out a 10-page questionnaire to be used by lawyers in examining potential jurors. Questions will cover employment, smoking histories and television-viewing habits.

Jury selection in another high-profile trial in Miami against tobacco companies -- Norma Broin vs. Philip Morris Cos Inc -- is now its fourth week, with the trial judge estimating testimony will not begin until July.
That class-action suit, filed on behalf of thousands of flight attendants, seeks damages from cigarette makers for illnesses allegedly caused by breathing secondhand smoke on U.S. passenger flights.
